title: SWE-agent: a coding harness that edits and runs programs
text: A coding harness wraps a language model with a file editor, a shell and a test runner so it can fix repository bugs. The harness scores patches automatically and the benchmark is SWE-bench Verified.

title: ToolBench: a benchmark for function calling with external tools
text: Function calling benchmarks record whether a model selects the right tool and fills its schema. ToolBench covers thousands of interfaces and measures argument correctness and call order.

title: AgentCoord: coordinating several autonomous workers on one goal
text: Multi-agent coordination assigns subtasks to distinct workers and merges their results. A planner broadcasts a shared plan and a dispatcher avoids duplicated effort.

title: MemGPT: memory that survives a long conversation
text: Long-term memory lets an assistant recall notes from earlier sessions by paging them into a small context window. A memory store ranks past notes and retrieves the relevant ones.

title: AgentBench: measuring progress of autonomous systems
text: Evaluation suites score whether a system improves at a task across many environments. AgentBench reports success rates and failure categories for each domain.

title: Sandboxing untrusted code generated by a model
text: A sandbox limits what a program can read or write, and permissions decide which capabilities the runtime may grant. Container isolation contains a misbehaving process.

title: WebVoyager: browsing the live web with a multimodal model
text: A browser controller clicks, scrolls and types on real websites. It must ground instructions in screenshots and recover when a page changes.

title: Model Context Protocol: a standard interface for tool servers
text: A tool protocol defines how a client discovers and calls external capabilities. Servers expose typed operations and the client negotiates the supported features.

title: Plan-and-Solve prompting for decomposed tasks
text: Planning breaks a goal into ordered steps before any action. A planner can revise the list when a step fails and a verifier checks the outcome.

title: Self-Refine: iterative correction with self feedback
text: Self-correction asks a system to critique its own answer and try again. Gains appear only when the critic is grounded in a checkable signal.

title: Budget-aware routing to control the cost of model calls
text: A router sends easy requests to a cheap model and hard ones to a strong model. A token budget stops spending once a run reaches its cap.

title: Human approval gates for high-impact assistant actions
text: Human-in-the-loop review pauses a workflow before a risky action and resumes it after approval. The reviewer sees the proposed action and its evidence.

title: Bots that triage pull requests and developer workflows
text: Developer bots label issues, summarise changes and request reviewers. They read repository events and post comments through an API.

title: Long-horizon tasks that need hundreds of steps
text: A long-horizon benchmark measures whether a system keeps its objective over many sequential actions. Error accumulation and context limits cause most failures.

title: Tracing and observability for agent runs
text: Observability records every model call, tool call and latency as a span. Traces expose where a run stalled or looped.

title: Defending agents against prompt injection in retrieved data
text: Prompt injection hides instructions in a web page or document that the model later reads. A defence labels untrusted content and refuses to follow instructions found inside it.

title: Retrieval pipelines that feed an agent fresh context
text: Retrieval for agents fetches passages at question time and ranks them before the model sees them. Hybrid search combines keyword and semantic matches.

title: Small language models as capable agents
text: A small model can act as an agent when the task is narrow and the harness supplies strong tools. Distillation and tool design recover much of the gap to a large model.

title: Detecting synthetic images with frequency fingerprints
text: Synthetic image detection looks for generator artefacts in the frequency domain. A classifier separates real photographs from generated ones.

title: Watermarking generated text so it can be traced
text: A watermark biases token choices with a secret key so a detector can later recover the signal. Provenance of machine written text depends on it.

title: Localising image manipulation with boundary artefacts
text: Manipulation localisation finds the edited region rather than only flagging the image. Boundary discontinuities and noise residuals reveal the splice.

title: Deepfake speech detection across unseen speakers
text: Spoofed speech detection must generalise to voices it never trained on. Front-end features and augmentation reduce the speaker shortcut.

title: Attacking provenance watermarks in generated images
text: A watermark attacker perturbs a generated image until the detector misses it. Robustness is measured against compression and cropping.

title: Attributing synthetic media to its generator
text: Generator attribution predicts which model produced an image. Fingerprints differ across diffusion and autoregressive families.

title: Sparse attention that keeps only the important tokens
text: Sparse attention reduces quadratic cost by attending to a subset of positions. Routing picks the keys that matter for each query.

title: State space models as an alternative to attention
text: A state space model scans a sequence with a fixed-size memory. It offers linear cost and strong long-range recall.

title: Mixture of experts with learned routing
text: A mixture of experts activates only a few feed-forward blocks per token. A router balances load and quality.

title: RoPE positional encodings and length generalisation
text: Rotary positional encodings inject position by rotating query and key vectors. Scaling the rotation extends context length.

title: Looped transformers that reuse the same layers
text: A looped transformer applies a shared block several times. Weight sharing increases depth without new parameters.

title: Subword tokenisation and vocabulary design
text: Subword tokenisation splits rare words into frequent pieces. Vocabulary size trades sequence length against embedding table size.

title: NimbusBench measures long tool chains
text: NimbusBench scores agents on long chains of tool calls.

title: PilotEval grades browser automation
text: PilotEval grades browser tasks step by step.

title: LedgerGuard detects budget overruns
text: LedgerGuard flags runs that exceed their budget.

title: Notes on agent benchmarks
text: What is it about the tools? For me it is about what an agent does with them, and what the benchmark measures.

title: Evaluating agents in the field
text: It is about what we can measure. For me, the question is what the tools do and how the agent responds.

title: Long tasks and tool chains
text: What is it about long tasks? For me it is about the tools, and about what the agent can do next.

title: Llama-3.1-8B as a compact agent backbone
text: The Llama-3.1-8B release is a small open model used as an agent backbone. Its size keeps serving cheap.

title: Qwen2.5-VL for visual grounding
text: Qwen2.5-VL reads screenshots and documents. The Qwen2.5 family adds visual grounding to an agent.

title: RAG/agentic systems that retrieve their own tools
text: A slash compound names the overlap of retrieval and agentic design. The system discovers tools through search.
